Put 2 cups of water in a saucepan and add the tomatoes, green pepper and onion. Bring to a boil.
Add the sambar powder, salt and tamarind pulp, and continue to boil until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the cooked dal and mix thoroughly. Adjust the consistency by adding more water (it should be thin).

In a small pan, heat the oil and add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek, asafoetida, turmeric, dried red chilies and curry leaves. (Optionally, add some finely chopped onion and saute until light brown.)
Add the tempering to the sambar, give it a good stir, and garnish with cilantro just before serving.

recipes.name: Sambar (Radish)

ingredients.prep_notes: peeled and sliced into rounds (about 3-4 medium white radishes)
large lemon-sized ball; soak in 1 cup warm water and squeeze for pulp

steps: Cook the dal: Rinse the toor dal and pressure cook with 5-6 water and turmeric . Mash it into a smooth paste once cooked.
Cook radish: In a large pot, add the sliced radish, chopped tomato, and enough water to cover them. Simmer until the radish is tender but not mushy (about 8-10 minutes).
Combine: Pour the tamarind extract and sambar powder into the pot with the vegetables. Let it boil for 5 minutes until the raw smell of tamarind disappears.
Simmer: Stir in the mashed dal. Adjust the consistency with hot water if too thick. Let the sambar simmer for another 5-10 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Tempering: Heat sesame oil in a small pan. Add fenugreek seeds, mustard seeds, cumin, red chilies, curry leaves, and hing. Pour the hot tempering directly into the sambar.
Garnish: Finish with freshly chopped coriander leaves

recipes.name: Sambar (Onion)
steps: Soak the tamarind in hot water for 1 hour. Squeeze it with your hands and remove the fiber, and then set aside, reserving the soaking water.
Thoroughly rinse the toor dal in water until the water is clear. Soak it in 3 cups of water and a pinch of asafoetida for 30-60 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot. Add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek, asafoetida, turmeric, dried red chilies and curry leaves, and saute for 5-7 seconds.
Add the onions and saute until translucent. Add the tomato and salt, and saute until the tomato is well cooked.
Add the sambar powder and saute for 1-2 minutes, then pour in the tamarind water and simmer over low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the cooked dal and stir to combine. Adjust the salt and sambar powder if needed.
Garnish with cilantro before serving.

recipes.name: Sambar (Varutharacha)

ingredients.prep_notes: medium, finely diced, for coconut paste

steps: Thaw the coconut to room temperature. Soak the tamarind in water for 1 hour.

Rinse the toor dal and soak it in water and a pinch of asafoetida for 1 hour. Place the soaked dal in a pot with water to cover and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until cooked, about 1 hour.
To make the coconut paste, roast all ingredients in a pan over medium heat, and then grind to a paste.
Make tamarind paste by squeezing the soaked tamarind with your hands and removing the fibers.

Add 1 1/2 cups of water to a saucepan along with the drumsticks, eggplants, tomato and onion. Bring to a boil and cook for 1-2 minutes. Add the tamarind paste and cooked dal. Once the raw smell of the tamarind is gone, add the coconut paste and salt, and simmer for a few minutes.

Make the tempering by heating the coconut oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds, fenugreek, dried red chilies, asafoetida and curry leaves and saute for 5-7 seconds. Pour the tempering into the sambar and adjust for salt.
Remove from the heat, cover and let the flavours mingle before garnishing with cilantro and serving.

recipes.name: Sambar Powder
steps: Dry roast the jeera and methi separately (without oil)
Roast all the other ingredients separately with a little bit of oil
Let it cool. Grind to a fine powder
Once its completely cooled store in airtight containers. Divide it into 4-5 identical containers

recipes.name: Simple Dal Tadka
steps: Wash Toor dal and soak for 1-2 hours
Pressure Cook dal with turmeric and a little salt (1:3 water ratio) and then whisk it to mix it well
Take about 20% of the dal aside for vegan serving
For the regular dal: bring the dal to a boil. Separately make a seasoning with ghee, jeera, hing, red chillies. Add to the dal and mix
Add lemon juice and chopped cilantro and switch off the flame
For vegan dal follow the same process but make the seasoning with oil instead of ghee

recipes.name: Sliced Carrots and Cucumber
steps: Slice Carrots and cucumbers in the food processor
Add salt, black pepper, and mix well
Add lemon juice concentrate
Garnish with cilantro

recipes.name: Spinach, Apple & Toasted Almond Salad
recipes.notes: Serve with Apple Cider Vinaigrette. Slice apples just before serving to prevent browning — toss in a little dressing (the cider vinegar keeps them white).

ingredients.prep_notes: large, crisp (Honeycrisp or Fuji), thinly sliced

steps: Toast Almonds: Heat almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until they are fragrant and lightly golden. Set aside to cool.
Make Dressing: blend together olive oil, apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, minced garlic, salt, and pepper
Assemble: combine the baby spinach, sliced cucumbers, and dried cranberries.
Add Apples:  Toss the apple slices in a little bit of the dressing beforehand; the acidity of the cider vinegar will keep them white.
Toss & Serve: Drizzle the remaining dressing over the salad and toss gently. Sprinkle the toasted almonds on top at the very end to keep them crunchy.

recipes.name: Sprouted Savory Moong with Khakhra
steps: Wash and soak moong for about 8 hours.
Drain, cover with cloth, and sprout for about 16-24 hours.
Cook sprouted moong with about twice the water, plus salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric, until soft.
Heat ghee and add mustard, cumin, asafoetida, remaining turmeric, ground coriander, and half the cilantro.
Turn off heat, add red chili powder, and mix.
Stir seasoning into cooked moong.
Add lemon/lime juice and remaining cilantro, then adjust salt.
Serve with khakhra.

recipes.name: Thai Curry with Vegetables & Tofu

ingredients.prep_notes: medium head, cut into bite sized florets
medium, cut into bite sized florets
1 pack, or fried tofu, cut into 1-inch cubes
as needed; curry pastes are typically salted

steps: Put a kettle on to boil.
Scoop out 2 tablespoons of thick coconut cream from the top of the canned coconut milk and add it to a pot over medium heat. Cook until it begins to release oil.
Add the curry paste and saute until fragrant. Add the broccoli and cauliflower, and stir.
Once the vegetables are somewhat tender, add the bamboo shoots and tofu and continue to saute.
After 5-7 minutes, but before the vegetables are fully done, add the red bell pepper and the remaining coconut milk. Simmer for a few minutes, taking care that the red pepper remains crunchy.
Add one half cup of the boiling water and mix well. Avoid overcooking.
Taste for salt and spice level. Add more curry paste if desired, and stir in the cilantro.
All vegetables should be cooked with a slight crunch and not be mushy.

recipes.name: Tomato Cucumber Romaine Salad
steps: Wash and dry cucumbers, tomatoes, lettuce and cilantro. Peel the cucumbers if they are waxy.
Cut cucumbers, tomatoes, lettuce into 1 inch bite sized cubes
Add salt, pepper, olive oil, lemon juice and mix well
Garnish with cilantro and serve

recipes.name: Tomato Salsa
steps: Chop the onions, garlic and jalapenos in a food processor. Lightly pulse the tomatoes in the food processor separately.
Finely chop the cilantro. Mix everything together in a bowl. Add salt, pepper, lemon juice and mix
Refrigerate it for a few hours before serving

recipes.name: Undhiyu
steps: Prep the vegetables: Quarter the eggplant vertically. Peel the outer green skin of plantain with a peeler, cut it vertically in half and 4 horizontal parts. Store covered in water.
Peel the sweet potato, cut it vertically in half and 3-4 horizontal parts so each part is about 1.5 inches long and wide. Store covered in water
Peel the potato and split them in 4 pieces, store in covered water. Thaw all the frozen vegetables.
Lightly pulse the coconut to make it into a rough powder. Make a coarse powder of sesame seeds.
In a bowl mix together the coconut, sesame seed powder, jeera and coriander powder, red chili powder, and salt.
Take a pot, add the oil. Lightly crush the ajwain in between your palms and add to the oil. Add some salt to taste
Layer all the vegetables with the eggplants and plantains on the top. Add plenty of water so it can cook without the vegetables getting stuck to the bottom of the pan
Cover the lid of the pot, and start the flame on medium and let the vegetables cook for 20-35 minutes
Add the coconut-sesame-spice mixture and mix well. Cover and continue to cook until the vegetables are cooked properly
Check for salt, add jaggery and the methi muthias and lightly mix. Cover and let it cook on low flame for 3-4 minutes
Garnish with cilantro and serve

recipes.name: Upma

ingredients.prep_notes: or Cream of Rice for GF

steps: Bring water to a boil in a separate pot.
Heat 1 1/2 tbsp ghee and saute chana dal for 1 minute.
Add urad dal and saute another minute.
Add fenugreek and mustard seeds; when mustard pops, add cumin and asafoetida and saute 1 minute.
Add green chilies, ginger, curry leaves, onion, and salt; saute until onion is translucent.
Add Cream of Wheat and roast on medium heat for 7-9 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and slowly add boiled water while stirring continuously.
Cover and cook on low for 2 minutes.
Stir in remaining ghee and lemon/lime juice.
Garnish with cilantro and serve (optionally with coconut chutney).

recipes.name: Varan Bhaat
recipes.notes: Maharashtra. V / GF. Rice & Plain Dal.
steps: Wash the toor dal a few times, then soak in a bowl of lukewarm water for 1-2 hours.

Once soaked, place the dal in a pot with fresh water, along with the turmeric and asafoetida and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer until soft, about 1 hour. Mash until smooth, adding hot water to adjust the consistency as needed (it should be pourable like sambar).
While the dal is cooking, wash the rice. Soak it in a pot with 2 cups of water for 15-30 minutes.

Bring the rice to a boil in its soaking water over medium heat, uncovered. Once most of the surface water is absorbed, cover and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook for 15 minutes (setting a timer may be helpful). Turn off the heat and let it sit for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Ghee can be added to the rice once it starts to boil.
Serve the rice topped with the dal along with a spoon of ghee and a quarter of lemon on the side.

recipes.name: Vegetable Pulav

ingredients.prep_notes: half a head medium, cut into medium florets

steps: Wash and soak the rice for 30 minutes, then drain.
Soak the saffron in 1 tablespoon warm water to let the flavor bloom, then add the coconut milk.
Grind or mash the chili paste ingredients together.
In a large pot, heat the oil. Add the cinnamon, bay leaves, cardamom and cloves, along with the onion. Saute until the onion is golden brown. Add the chili paste and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the pureed tomato, half the mint and half the cilantro, and cook for 1 minute.
Add the kasuri methi, the cauliflower, green peas, green beans and salt, and stir to combine.
Cover the pot and cook over medium heat until the vegetables are almost done, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the water and coconut milk (with saffron), along with the remaining cilantro and mint. Mix well to combine.

Add the drained rice and cook over medium heat until the water is absorbed. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and cook for about 15 minutes. Check occasionally that the rice isn't sticking to the pan.
Switch off the heat and let the pulav sit for about 10 minutes before removing the lid.
Fluff with a spatula or fork, being careful to not break the rice grains.

recipes.name: Ven Pongal (Khara Pongal)
recipes.notes: South India. V/GF. Savory rice and moong dal porridge with ghee tempering. Source: hebbarskitchen.com
steps: Prepare 4/1 quantities of regular vs vegan pongal. Only difference in the two versions is that regular version uses ghee for tempering and the vegan version uses coconut oil.
Wash the rice and dal, add water and let it soak for 30 minutes (if time allows).
Start cooking in an open pot on medium flame. Once water is almost absorbed, cover with low flame for 15 minutes.
Stir the cooked mixture until it is a thick consistency (like cooked oatmeal).
Roughly crush the black pepper.
Prepare tempering by heating up ghee, adding jeera, hing, black pepper, curry leaves, and ginger.
Add the tempering to the rice and dal mixture and add salt to taste.

recipes.name: Vermicelli Payasam
steps: Warm 1-2 tablespoons of the milk. Crush the saffron lightly between your fingers and add to the milk. Soak for about an hour.
Place the remaining milk in a pot and bring to a boil over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally to prevent scalding.
Meanwhile in a saucepan, heat the ghee over low heat and roast the cashews and raisins until they are golden brown and the raisins puff up, being careful not to burn them. Remove and set aside.
In the same saucepan, add the vermicelli and roast for 3-5 minutes until it turns golden brown. Add 1 cup water and cook until the vermicelli is tender.
Add the cooked vermicelli to the boiling milk and mix. Continue to cook, stirring frequently, for 10-15 minutes until the vermicelli softens and the payasam thickens to a creamy consistency.
Mix in the sugar and allow it to dissolve. Taste for sweetness and add more sugar if desired.
Boil the mixture over low heat until the payasam reaches the desired consistency. Then add the roasted cashews and raisins.
Switch off the heat, add the cardamom and soaked saffron milk, and mix well.
Payasam is served warm, but is also delicious cold.

recipes.name: Wheat Laddu
steps: serve alongside the meal

recipes.name: Yellow Cucumber Pickle
steps: Wash the yellow cucumbers and wipe dry. Remove the seeds and cut into 1/2 inch pieces, skin included.
Toss them in a bowl with the red chili powder, salt, mustard powder, roasted fenugreek powder and turmeric, and mix well.
Add the oil and mix once again. Cover and let sit in a cool, dry spot for 12-24 hours to allow the flavors to meld.
Store in a clean, dry glass container in the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Yellow Moong Dal Masala Palak Khichdi
recipes.notes: North India. V / GF. Spiced Spinach Khichdi.

ingredients.prep_notes: or small bag of baby spinach, washed and chopped

steps: Wash the rice and moong dal.
Blend the ginger and green chilies together to make a coarse paste.

In a deep pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Once hot, lower the heat, add the cloves and cinnamon and allow them to sizzle. Add the cumin seeds, asafoetida, dried red chilies and turmeric. Saute for a few seconds before adding the chili paste.

Add the washed dal and rice and saute for 4-5 minutes. Pour in the water and cook uncovered over medium heat until the dal and rice are done and the consistency is thick like porridge, but not dry (add a little water if necessary).
Add the ground coriander, ground cumin, red chili powder and salt, and mix well.
Add the lemon juice and spinach. Cook until the spinach wilts slightly -- it should be bright green and not fully cooked. Switch off the heat. The remaining heat will cook the spinach.
Garnish with ghee.

recipes.name: Zucchini Sabzi with Green Pepper
steps: Quarter the zucchini across its length and chop into 1 cm thin sllices. Chop the green pepper and onion into 1 inch pieces
Heat mustard oil in the pot until it is smoking. Once smoking, reduce the heat. Add panch phoran and let it sizzle.
Add onions, curry leaves, turmeric, hing, and red chilly powder. Add green pepper and zucchini and saute on medium-high flame
Add salt to taste. At this stage zucchini will release water
Cook on medium high flame until the zucchini is ccooked and most of the water evaporates. Keep turning in the interim to prevent it from burning
Add garam masala and cilantro and give it a good mix. And you are done!

recipes.name: Zucchini Sabzi with tomato
steps: Quarter the zucchini across its length and chop into 1 cm thin sllices. Roughly chop the tomato into 1 inch pieces
Heat mustard oil in the pot until it is smoking. Once smoking, reduce the heat. Add panch phoran and let it sizzle. Add garlic, curry leaves, turmeric, hing, and red chilly powder
Add tomato and zucchini and saute on medium-high flame. Add salt to taste. At this stage zucchini will release water
Cook on medium high flame until the zucchini and tomato is cooked and most of the water evaporates. Keep turning in the interim to prevent it from burning
Add garam masala and cilantro and give it a good mix. And you are done!
